The bananas that we eat are sterile anyway.

Dairy generally does kill an animal, just in a less direct way.

For a cow to lactate, you have to make it produce a calf once a year, and then remove that calf. At the moment, that calf is often killed, as we don't need as many as would be produced. If we kept and looked after every calf, we'd never be able to afford milk prices. (and by extension, cheese, butter, cream, etc.)

Chickens, even free range, are killed after 18 months or so, when they start to lay less than one egg a day, again for financial reasons. The male chicks that you get when you're breeding those laying hens in the first place get fed into a grinder at a couple of days old.
